details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:1066 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The security exemption in process_block (`if (lens == "SECURITY & INPUT VALIDATION" || lens == "IMPLICIT-EXECUTION & TRUST-BOUNDARY RISKS" || file == "") { exempt = 1 }`) needs an exact, case-sensitive LENS match, and scripts/review_parse_consolidator.sh passes the LENS text through without normalising it; test_convergence_floor_and_security_exemptions (tests/test_review_issue_ledger.py:794) asserts that a lowercase lens does not block.
  WHY: From round 3 on, a lone security finding whose lens is spelled differently is reclassified advisory-lone and the editor is told "Make no edits for them", which breaks the rule that security findings always block (AD-2); all reviewers rated this MAJOR.
- prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt:33 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The added CONVERGENCE ADVISORY NOTES bullet takes this DEFAULT-tier prompt to 251 lines, over the 250-line limit at tests/prompt_size_budget.py line 14.
  WHY: The required `quick / static-checks` job already fails ("251 lines exceeds DEFAULT limit of 250", run 45459992755), so the PR cannot merge; all four reviewers rated it BLOCKER, and minimax_minimax-m3 raised it only as a hardening suggestion (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE 5).
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:1046-1064 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Once any FLAGGED_BY token matches a reviewer section (`named_any`), only named sections are counted (`if (sup[s] && (!named_any || named[s]))`), so a reviewer whose own file independently supports the finding is left out when the consolidator did not list it.
  WHY: A finding that two or more reviewers raised can be demoted to advisory-lone and withheld from the editor, which goes against the requirement that the count be verified from the per-reviewer files; all reviewers rated this MAJOR.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1497-1506 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The REVIEW CONVERGENCE directive (line 1502, "Make no edits for them") has no carve-out for CI failures in PR_CHECK_RUNS_CONTEXT_FILE, and the classifier has no CI-derived exemption; it conflicts with the "FIX EVERY RUN" CI section at lines 1586-1588.
  WHY: In round 3 or later, a CI failure anchored by only one reviewer can be classified advisory-lone and left unfixed, which violates "A CI failure on the head always blocks"; all reviewers rated this MAJOR.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:754-761 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The mktemp, gawk and stats-parse failure paths (calls at 788-790 and 1197-1210) call `review_convergence_log 0 0 0 error`, so the log reports `outcome=approve` although classification was not applied and review_issues.txt still blocks.
  WHY: The contractual REVIEW_CONVERGENCE log line reports an approval exactly when classification failed, which misleads the rollout metrics and any downstream log readers; all reviewers rated this NIT.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:252-267 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The awk `NF >= 7 && n < 50` caps the "Not blocking (one reviewer)" comment at 50 advisory rows and adds no overflow marker.
  WHY: On large PRs, lone findings after the 50th are silently left out of the PR comment, which goes against "never dropped silently"; severity is disputed (sonnet NIT, minimax MAJOR), so the highest is used.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:1030 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In the anchor support check, `lo - tolerance` is 0 or negative for findings at lines 1-3, so the reviewers say the lower bound has no effect and anchors elsewhere in the same file count as support.
  WHY: The reviewer count for top-of-file findings may be inflated, which changes the blocking/advisory result; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly dispute this, saying `anc_line <= hi + tolerance` still applies.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:review_convergence_load_config | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_AUTOFIX_COUNT is unset, the round silently falls back to ITERATION; minimax says the step that calls the ledger does not set the variable, which is set only at `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3552` and `4007`.
  WHY: The round may resolve wrongly (gemini: the rule applies too early in round 1; minimax: `reason=disabled_round`, so the rule is effectively off); anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash dispute this, saying the editor step exports the variable and ITERATION equals count+1.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:1114-1118 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The bundle parser compares a byte count (`wc -c` in scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:910-919) against length($0), which counts characters in a multibyte locale.
  WHY: With UTF-8 reviewer output, sections can be missed or merged and support miscounted, so a multi-reviewer finding may become advisory-lone; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes this, citing `LC_ALL=C` exported at review_issue_ledger.sh line 4.
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:84-561 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: ISSUE_START_RE (`^=== ISSUE ([0-9]+) ===$`, line 84; used at 355 and 558-561) does not match the `=== ADVISORY ISSUE N ===` stubs written by review_convergence_stub_advisory_blocks (scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:1260-1265).
  WHY: Advisory findings are left out of review_findings_record.json, and an all-advisory round records consolidator.ran=false / issues_file_no_blocks; severity is disputed (sonnet and luna NIT, glm MAJOR), so the highest is used, and the file is outside files_touched.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_partial_finalize.sh:152-159 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: review_convergence_advisory.txt is missing from the persisted runtime artifact lists (lines 152-159 and 374-383), but on a same-head resume the ledger stage is skipped and review_issues.txt is restored with the ADVISORY stubs already in it.
  WHY: The resumed run renders ADVISORY stubs with no convergence directive and no "Not blocking (one reviewer)" comment section, so the editor may fix lone findings anyway.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:253 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `clean()` does not strip the markdown link characters `[`, `]`, `(`, `)` from the reviewer-derived lens and summary fields.
  WHY: Reviewer-controlled text can inject markdown links into a PR comment that is posted with pipeline credentials.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:1349-1756 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The two calls to review_convergence_stub_advisory_blocks (after the REVIEW_LEDGER_ENABLED=0 early exit and after the residual rewrite) could see a stale advisory file from an earlier run if the switch is toggled; the reviewer says "No actual bug, just close."
  WHY: The byte-identical switch-off test covers only a single round, so the stale-file case is untested; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes the stale-file concern because RUNTIME_DIR is per run.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:358-368 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The prior-ledger TSV reader (~line 1503) now reads 11 columns (`prior_convergence`), so 10-column rows from older cached ledgers misalign.
  WHY: A restored pre-change ledger cache fills PRIOR_OUTCOMES with corrupted data and display_outcomes renders gibberish; test_convergence_prior_ledger_lines_are_not_reset writes only the 11-column format.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
